messages.subject: VEI
messages.body_plain:
Hello tidyLPA team,

I am using the tidyLPA package and I would like to use the VEI model mentioned in mclust. Is there a way to run that model through tidyLPA?
Of the diagonal models only VVI and EEI seem possible, according to the tutorial.

Kind regards,

Calum

messages.subject: Re: VEI
messages.body_plain:
Hi Calum (and JD), sorry, I’ve caused confusion by making a mistake.

Yes, as you both indicate, mclust can fit the VEI model (?mclust::mclustModelNames() confirms this):

VEI"

diagonal, varying volume, equal shape

JD, you note that this model can be fit in MPlus. Can you confirm how the variances and covariances would be estimated for such a model (i.e., what is freely-estimated, what is constrained to be equal between classes, and what is allowed to vary between classes)?

Calum, my understanding is that the negative BIC is due to a difference in the sign in the formula. See discussion here: https://github.com/data-edu/tidyLPA/issues/86

Josh

--

Joshua M. Rosenberg, Ph.D.
Assistant Professor, STEM Education

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville

messages.subject: Re: VEI
messages.body_plain:
Josh:

I mentioned it could be executed in Mclust (not sure about Mplus). As for the negative BIC value, you are correct in that it is a change in the sign formula. Aside from minor differences between Mclust and Mplus for other models, whether it is a positive or negative BIC does not negate the point that model fit [whether Mplus or Mclust (for those models that both can fit) is used] will be virtually identical.

Best regards,
J.D.

messages.subject: Re: VEI
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for clarifying – and, oye, yes, I see you meant mclust.

Calum, we deliberately have constrained which models can be fit in tidyLPA to only include those that are the most common (at least in the social sciences – and as a part of analyses that go by the name Latent Profile Analysis). And, so, we do not have a plan to make the VEI model you mentioned able to be estimated via tidyLPA.

Josh

--

The University of Tennessee, Knoxville

messages.body_plain:
To whom it might regard,

Dear Joshua, maybe a year ago I found this web page, that helped me to get through a Latent Profile analysis with Rstudio, https://joshuamrosenberg.com/blog/lpa-in-r-using-mclust/. But today, the page is not available anymore, and something I managed to do easily a year ago, now seems to not be working.  Just with this simple script it did wonders.

m2<-estimate_profiles(Decision_making,

                      Honest_Hum, Emotionality, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Opp_E, Machiavellianism, Psyhcopathy, Narcissism,

                      n_profiles = 2)

I know is a long shot, and probably you won’t answer. But I am going crazy here, and I though I would give it a try. Since I do not understand why something that worked perfectly a year ago, now seems to now be working. Maybe I am doing something wrong, and since I was capable of getting there with your great explanation, I though I might ask.

Thank you in advance, and sorry for the inconvenience,

Kind regards, Ona Dominguez

messages.subject: "Mclust could not estimate model" error - Ability for tidyLPA/mclust to handle variables with multiple zero values?
messages.subject_clean: "Mclust could not estimate model" error - Ability for tidyLPA/mclust to handle variables with multiple zero values?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josh and Caspar,

While running tidyLPA, I've been encountering errors informing me that "Mclust could not estimate model X, even when it was just for one variable and 2 clusters (model 2). I noticed that when I removed the zero values from the variable, the code managed to fit models up to 4 classes before the same error occurred, hence my question: Is mclust/tidyLPA limited in any way to only be able to classify variables without zero values? Is there any way to tackle this problem?

Thanks and Best Regards,
Yi Ting
